faq.q: What does "subject to court approval" mean for my offer?
faq.a: Where the court has directed sale by contract conditional on the approval of the court (Rule 13-5 (4) (b)), the person with conduct of sale applies under Rule 21-7 (9) for an order confirming the sale, directing the proceeds and vesting title in the purchaser — until that order, the sale is not final.

faq.q: Can someone outbid my accepted offer?
faq.a: The court's sale directions may define the rights of a person to bid, make offers or meet bids (Rule 13-5 (4) (d)), and the Supreme Court's practice direction PD-66 governs foreclosure proceedings — so a competing bid at the approval stage is a real possibility in this process.

faq.q: What is a court-ordered sale in Langley?
faq.a: It is a sale of a property supervised by the court after a lender has taken legal action, and the sale needs court approval. Offers are usually made subject to that approval, and other buyers can sometimes bid higher at the hearing.

faq.q: Can I put conditions on an offer for a foreclosure in Langley?
faq.a: Conditions such as financing or inspection may be limited or not accepted, depending on the lender's and the court's terms. Speak to Jared and your lawyer before you write an offer.
